title: voids: two void distributions, fresh random numbers
purpose: Exercises `voids`, which maps the cavities of a configuration [@epsrmanual]: the box is divided into cubic pixels, pixels within `radius` of an atom are occupied, connected unoccupied pixels are labelled as voids, and the void-size histogram, the pair correlation of void pixels (and its inter-void part) and the void volume fraction are written. This case tests a single run with two distributions, the `include` list and a reset random-number generator.
system: Analysed configuration: `200DMSO400Water.ato`, an unchanged copy of the EPSR-test box of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO; atom types S, O, C, H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1): 3200 atoms, DMSO mole fraction 1/3, 300 K, cubic box of side 33.1213 Å (0.0881 atoms/Å³), the EPSR model of the deuterated DMSO-water neutron data (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), cf. [@soperluzar1992]. Distribution 1: all atoms occupy the pixels within 2.0 Å. Distribution 2: radius 2.5 Å with `include O1 H1 XX`: only water atoms occupy pixels and occupied/unoccupied are swapped (`XX`, absent from the `.ato` file, is silently dropped). The grid is adjusted to the radius (99³ pixels, README); the pixel correlation is sampled from 100 random origins with the Park-Miller generator with Bays-Durham shuffle [@parkmiller1988,@numrec1992].
inputs: `cavity.VOIDS.dat`: `nsize 100`, `npix 100`, `voidmax 500.0`, `nsumt 0`, the two distributions above (blank `include` for the first); no `randomno.dat`; `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied unchanged from EPSR-test.
verification: Single pass. Without `randomno.dat` the generator is reset (idum = 0) and the file is created and saved. Compared: `cavity.VOIDS.n01` (three columns with spreads per distribution), the rewritten `cavity.VOIDS.dat`, `fort.14` and `randomno.dat`. The reference `fort.14` gives fractions of pixels 0.07696 (distribution 1) and 0.62561 (distribution 2).
notes: Fortran quirks reproduced: the blank `include` value is written back using the word boundaries of the previous keyword (3 blanks), and nsumt and ndist are stored into the `npix` and `voidmax` entries (reference `.dat`: `npix 1`, `voidmax 2`).
